sections.what_are_the_complications_of_amyloidosi:
The disorder is known to have serious complications. If the accumulation of protein occurs in kidney, then it may cause kidney failure. While, if the deposition occurs in heart, then heart may get little difficulty in pumping the blood and in turn may get enlarged. In short, there may occur heart failure. So, treatment is necessary. 
 HOW CAN AMYLOIDOSIS BE DIAGNOSED? 
 Early diagnosis of the disorder will help to prevent further damage to the organ. Blood test and urine test can help to get any information about the abnormal protein. A patient may be asked to for liver function test and thyroid test as well depending on the symptoms. Echocardiogram can be done to confirm heart functioning. Biopsy of a suspected organ can confirm the diagnosis.
